Hero.title: Building a <accent>Connected</accent>, <accent>Open</accent>, and <accent>Resilient</accent> Climate Ecosystem for West and Central Africa
Hero.description: WACREN CLI-MET leverages advanced digital connectivity, open science, and trusted research infrastructure to strengthen climate research, climate-informed decision-making, and sustainable development across the region — positioning Research and Education Networks as critical enablers of climate resilience.
Hero.slide1_desc: Building a connected, open and resilient climate ecosystem in West and Central Africa
Hero.slide2_desc: Leveraging advanced digital connectivity, open science and trusted research infrastructure to support research, climate decision-making and sustainable development.

WhyItMatters.title: WACREN CLI-MET
WhyItMatters.p1: West and Central Africa is among the world's most climate-vulnerable regions. Escalating floods in the Sahel, prolonged droughts across the Lake Chad Basin, sea-level rise threatening coastal cities, and erratic rainfall devastating smallholder agriculture. These are not future risks. They are today's realities, affecting hundreds of millions of people. Climate challenges in West and Central Africa are inherently regional, yet the data, tools, and infrastructure needed to address them remain dangerously fragmented.
WhyItMatters.p2: National meteorological and hydrological services across the region are often under-resourced, working with outdated equipment and limited access to Earth Observation data. Climate research institutions and universities lack the computing infrastructure to run regional climate models. Agricultural agencies advising millions of smallholder farmers have no reliable pipeline of timely, localised agro-meteorological data.
WhyItMatters.p3: WACREN CLI-MET exists to close this gap by making high-quality, timely climate data accessible, shareable, and actionable across the region through a trusted, African-led research and education network infrastructure.
WhyItMatters.c1_desc: National meteorological agencies lack reliable, high-speed access to EUMETCast satellite data, global reanalysis products, and real-time sensor networks, leaving critical forecasting gaps.
WhyItMatters.c2_desc: Climate data remains locked in national silos with weak cross-border data-sharing protocols, preventing the regional-scale analysis that transboundary climate hazards demand.
WhyItMatters.c3_desc: Without access to HPC infrastructure and climate modelling platforms, regional scientists cannot generate the climate projections and scenario analyses essential for evidence-based policy.
WhyItMatters.c4_desc: Climate-dependent sectors, particularly food and water systems, lack the localised, real-time environmental data needed to protect livelihoods and guide resource management decisions.
WhyItMatters.opportunity_quote: Connectivity is the multiplier that turns climate data into climate action.
WhyItMatters.opportunity_text: WACREN's existing regional backbone is uniquely positioned to become the climate data highway that West and Central Africa urgently needs.

Pillars.section_lead: Each pillar of WACREN CLI-MET reinforces the others, creating a coherent system where connectivity, data, tools, science, and skills work together.
Pillars.p1_pt1: Federated access to EUMETCast, Earth Observation, and national meteorological datasets
Pillars.p1_pt2: FAIR-aligned data services (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable)
Pillars.p1_pt3: Integration with WACREN-connected data centres, clouds, and HPC resources
Pillars.p2_pt1: High-speed backbone interconnecting NRENs and research institutions
Pillars.p2_pt2: Secure cross-border data flows for climate modelling and early-warning systems
Pillars.p2_pt3: Redundant, resilient Points of Presence for critical climate services
Pillars.p3_pt1: LoRaWAN gateways integrated into NREN and campus networks
Pillars.p3_pt2: WMO-compliant automatic weather stations for real-time observation
Pillars.p3_pt3: Low-power sensors for rainfall, temperature, air & water quality
Pillars.p3_pt4: Solar-powered, resilient deployments for remote locations
Pillars.p4_pt1: Implementation of UNESCO Open Science principles for climate research
Pillars.p4_pt2: Shared platforms for data publishing, repositories, and collaboration
Pillars.p4_pt3: Open tools, open standards, and reproducible climate research workflows
Pillars.p5_pt1: Training in climate data analysis, HPC, and open data practices
Pillars.p5_pt2: Hands-on LoRaWAN deployment, sensor calibration, and data stewardship
Pillars.p5_pt3: Support for early-career researchers and women in climate STEM
Pillars.p5_pt4: Design sprints linked to real policy and sector needs

Flagship.section_lead: Concrete, partner-supported activities that bring the CLI-MET vision to life, producing tangible outcomes for the region.
Flagship.a1_title: EUMETCast Terrestrial Data Portal Deployment & Training
Flagship.a1_desc: Deploying and operationalising terrestrial EUMETCast receiving stations at National Meteorological and Hydrological Services, and providing training to ensure effective use of satellite-derived Earth Observation data across the WACREN region.
Flagship.a2_title: Open Climate & Agriculture Data Design Sprints
Flagship.a2_desc: Collaborative design sprints co-organised with EUMETSAT, WASCAL, ICTP, RUFORUM, and AfriGEO, bringing together meteorologists, agronomists, data scientists, and policymakers to develop open, actionable climate and agricultural data products for the region.
Flagship.a3_title: Regional Climate Research Connectivity & HPC Integration
Flagship.a3_desc: Connecting national and regional climate research centres to high-performance computing infrastructure through WACREN's high-speed backbone, enabling regional climate modelling, seasonal forecasting, and shared computing resources for complex climate simulations.
Flagship.a4_title: IoT & WMO-Compliant Environmental Monitoring Station Network
Flagship.a4_desc: Deployment of LoRaWAN-enabled, WMO-compliant automatic weather and environmental monitoring stations at WACREN-connected institutions, producing continuous, ground-truth observations that feed regional climate platforms.

Alignment.section_lead: CLI-MET is designed from the ground up to align with, and accelerate progress toward, the most important international and African climate and development frameworks.
Alignment.a1_desc: EU-funded research and education network connectivity underpinning CLI-MET's regional backbone infrastructure.
Alignment.a2_desc: FAIR data principles and open collaboration frameworks applied to climate research across the WACREN region.
Alignment.a3_desc: Contributing to a digitally integrated, science-driven, and resilient Africa through regional climate data infrastructure.
Alignment.a4_desc: Zero Hunger, Clean Water, Clean Energy, and Climate Action — all advanced by CLI-MET's integrated data and connectivity programme.

Footer.about: WACREN CLI-MET is the West and Central African Research and Education Network's regional programme for climate and meteorological infrastructure, building the digital backbone for a climate-resilient Africa.
Footer.attribution: The WACREN CLI-MET Program is supported by the AfricaConnect Project co-funded by the European Union through the Global Gateway Program.

Community.section_lead: CLI-MET serves a broad ecosystem of institutions whose effectiveness depends on reliable, shared climate data and infrastructure.
Community.b1_desc: Better data, better forecasts, better early warnings, with access to EUMETCast, LoRaWAN ground truth, and shared HPC resources.
Community.b2_desc: Shared transboundary data infrastructure enables coherent regional monitoring of river basins, ecosystems, and cross-border climate hazards.
Community.b3_desc: Agro-climate data pipelines support crop modelling, food system resilience research, and evidence-based advisory services for smallholders.
Community.b4_desc: Researchers gain access to open datasets, HPC facilities, and collaborative platforms, enabling globally competitive climate science from within the region.
Community.b5_desc: Decision-makers access coherent, evidence-based climate intelligence to underpin national adaptation plans, NDCs, and sectoral investment strategies.
Community.b6_desc: Institutions like EUMETSAT, EUREF, ICTP, WASCAL, and AfriGEO gain a trusted regional partner for data distribution, ground-truth collection, and capacity development.

Precursor.section_lead: The precursor phase established a foundation of national and regional collaborations and partnerships serving as building blocks and leading up to the current phase of the CLI-MET programme.
Precursor.p1_title: WACREN Climate Programme: Catalysing Climate Solutions
Precursor.p1_desc: Initial description, justification and partnerships for the WACREN CLI-MET programme
Precursor.p2_desc: Collaborating to conduct real-time monitoring of surface water pollution using IoT-based sensors
Precursor.p3_title: WACREN-ITCP Collaboration with GMet and GARNET
Precursor.p3_desc: A workshop as part of a developing program to boost the deployment of sensor networks and LoraWAN gateways in WACREN NRENs for climate and weather research support services

Impact.section_lead: Measurable, meaningful outcomes for researchers, policymakers, communities, and the region's climate future.
Impact.i1_title: Faster, More Reliable Climate Data Access
Impact.i1_text: Researchers, meteorologists, and policymakers gain high-speed, dependable access to satellite, in-situ, and modelled climate data, cutting the time from data collection to decision-making.
Impact.i2_text: Localised agro-meteorological intelligence supports better seasonal planning, pest and disease early warning, and resilient crop management, protecting the livelihoods of millions of farmers.
Impact.i3_text: Enhanced regional early-warning infrastructure, powered by real-time sensor networks and shared climate models, reduces the death toll and economic losses from floods, droughts, and extreme weather.
Impact.i4_text: A sustainable, open, and African-owned climate data platform, reducing dependence on external systems, building lasting institutional capacity, and positioning the region as a contributor to global climate science.

SDGs.section_title: Meeting the SDGs & Africa's Climate Commitments
SDGs.section_lead: WACREN CLI-MET is foundational infrastructure that accelerates progress on the region's most critical global and continental obligations.
SDGs.sdg2: Zero Hunger. Real-time agro-meteorological data from LoRaWAN weather stations and EUMETCast feeds directly supports early warning of drought, flood risk, and crop stress, enabling timely interventions that protect food security.
SDGs.sdg6: Clean Water & Sanitation. Hydrological monitoring stations and cross-border data sharing enable better river basin management, groundwater monitoring, and early warning of flood events.
SDGs.sdg7: Affordable & Clean Energy. High-resolution climate and solar radiation data support renewable energy resource assessment, hydropower planning, and climate-smart energy infrastructure investment.
SDGs.sdg13: Climate Action. CLI-MET is the core infrastructure for regional climate action, enabling National Adaptation Plans, strengthening NDCs, and giving African scientists the data and tools to drive evidence-based climate policy.
SDGs.sdg17: Partnerships for the Goals. CLI-MET operationalises multi-stakeholder partnerships between universities, regional bodies, EUMETSAT, WASCAL, ICTP, RUFORUM, and AfriGEO, pooling expertise to achieve shared climate outcomes.
SDGs.au1: AU Digital Transformation Strategy (2020–2030). CLI-MET is a direct embodiment of the AU DTS goal to deploy continental digital public infrastructure for science and development.
SDGs.au2: Comprehensive Africa Agriculture Development Programme. By delivering localised, timely agro-climate data to agricultural research institutions, CLI-MET directly underpins CAADP's goal of agriculture-led growth and food security.
SDGs.au3: Pan-African Climate Justice Alliance. CLI-MET strengthens Africa's scientific capacity and data sovereignty, ensuring the continent speaks from evidence in global climate negotiations.
SDGs.p1_text: CLI-MET is anchored within the AfricaConnect4 framework, leveraging EU Global Gateway investment to build the research connectivity backbone.
SDGs.p2_text: CLI-MET implements UNESCO's Open Science principles across climate research, making African climate knowledge globally accessible and reusable.

Champions.hero_title: The WACREN Climate Leadership, Innovation, Mentorship and Bridging (CLIMB)
Champions.hero_lead: Linking doctoral researchers in climate, agriculture, and health across to the data, computing power, mentorship and networks that will help translate knowledge to real impact.
Champions.gap_p1: West and Central Africa produces a steady stream of doctoral researchers working on climate systems, agriculture, land use, human habitat and economics, many of them through the West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adjusted Land Use (WASCAL), which spans twelve member countries.
Champions.gap_p2: WACREN CLIMB responds to the need for a structured way for these researchers to <bold>connect across borders, access regional data and computing resources</bold>, and reach platforms such as the Group on Earth Observations (GEO), AfriGEO and the UN Climate Change Conference.
Champions.launch_card_desc: Advances WACREN's support for research and infrastructure in the region, with support from the European Commission under the AfricaConnect4 project
Champions.network_lead: WACREN CLIMB will recruit 60 doctoral fellows from WACREN member institutions, with WASCAL's existing doctoral cohorts providing the initial anchor.
Champions.c1_desc: Shared access to WACREN's data and computing infrastructure and a cross-border peer community spanning countries and disciplines.
Champions.c2_desc: Co-developed with GEO, AfriGEO and WASCAL to turn real-time climate data into predictive models and decision-support tools for agriculture, water resources, energy and health.
Champions.c3_desc: WACREN-hosted side events at major forums, starting with COP31 in Antalya in November 2026 and continuing through the GEO Symposium and Plenary cycle.
Champions.c4_desc: Recognition of at least 20 outstanding fellows and workshop alumni as regional ambassadors for climate data and NREN infrastructure.
Champions.infra_title: Built on Infrastructure Already in Development
Champions.infra_lead: WACREN CLIMB builds on infrastructure that WACREN and its member national research and education networks (NRENs) are already developing.
Champions.infra_1_desc: WMO-compliant weather stations linked by LoRaWAN IoT gateways, extending pilots in Ghana and Nigeria into a regional climate monitoring platform.
Champions.infra_2_desc: A forthcoming data portal that will give African researchers and national meteorological agencies direct access to terrestrial data streams from EUMETSAT satellites.
Champions.infra_3_desc: WACREN's federated high-performance computing capacity, linked to global initiatives through the ZAOXI connection, enabling African institutions to process data locally.
Champions.milestone_1_desc: Launched at the 10th AfriGEO Symposium in Abuja; the call for fellows opens this quarter.
Champions.milestone_2_desc: First WACREN-hosted WACREN CLIMB side event.
Champions.milestone_3_desc: Continued side events at major forums.
Champions.partners_lead: WACREN CLIMB is jointly governed by regional and continental leaders in research, Earth observation, and climate services.
Champions.align_title: Aligned with Continental and Global Priorities
Champions.align_lead: WACREN CLIMB offers GEO Youth's African participants and WASCAL's doctoral alumni a regional home backed by research and education network infrastructure.
Champions.align_1_desc: Part of GEO's recent investment in the next generation of Earth observation practitioners.
Champions.align_3_desc: Places climate and resilience at its centre.
